title: African elephant poaching mortality rate, 2011 peak vs. 2017

source.name: African elephant poaching rates correlate with local poverty, national corruption and global ivory price
source.publisher: Hauenstein et al., Nature Communications (2019), using CITES MIKE data

notes: The study found the annual poaching mortality rate peaked above 10% in 2011 and fell below 4% by 2017. A separate 2020 analysis argues the decline was concentrated in Eastern Africa and poaching remained elevated elsewhere — noted here for balance.
